answer_summary: The current runtime executable baseline consists of a single GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/gemini-chat.yml), a configuration file (ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/config.json), and a Node.js controller (ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/send-to-gemini.js). Execution is triggered exclusively on push to main affecting nextmessage/nextmessage.json. The runtime deterministically parses steps from Agents.md headings, validates the triggering execution against strict role and step-specific schemas (Steps 0–4), extracts empirical path/SHA claims from the execution return to verify workspace files and local Git objects, constructs an immutable ground-truth findings report, and injects it into a Gemini API call (model default gemini-3.8-flash via REST v1beta generateContent). The supervisory response is subjected to a deterministic shape and role validation loop (up to 4 attempts), enforcing that any blocking ground-truth finding forbids a PASS gate. Upon PASS, the machine advances to the next step or marks the run 'complete'; upon FAIL, it preserves the current step with reason supervisory_gate_fail. Results are persisted to runs/<run_nonce>/{state.json, messages.json, store/store.json} and committed/pushed back to main by the workflow bot.

historical_facts.statement: gemini-chat.yml triggers on pushes to the main branch whose changed paths include ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/nextmessage/nextmessage.json, runs under concurrency group 'gemini-supervisor-state-machine' with cancel-in-progress disabled, and requests write permissions for contents.

The workflow sets up Node.js version 22 and executes 'node ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/send-to-gemini.js' with environment variables GEMINI_API_KEY and GEMINI_MODEL sourced from GitHub Actions repository variables (${{ vars.GEMINI_API_KEY }} and ${{ vars.GEMINI_MODEL }}), not from secrets.

After send-to-gemini.js executes, the workflow stages only 'ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/runs', extracts trigger run_nonce, step, and transition value using an inline Node script, and commits with message 'Gemini Supervisor checkpoint: <run_nonce> Step <step> <gate>' before pushing to origin HEAD:main.

send-to-gemini.js checks that ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/config.json exists, reads trigger_file, agents_file, runs_directory, and external_files.step3_evaluation_artifact.path (falling back to hardcoded default paths if unset), but does not validate or consume the config keys 'version', 'description', or 'external_files.step3_evaluation_artifact.keys'.

send-to-gemini.js requires run_nonce to match /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/, extracts numerical step IDs from Agents.md using regex /^## Step\s+(\d+)\s*$/gm, and initializes runs/<nonce> containing state.json, messages.json, and store/store.json if none exist, or verifies consistency across all three files if existing.

Every execution return schema must contain an object defining role_required === 'ChatGPT model', role_forbidden === 'Gemini model', role_completed === 'ChatGPT model', non-empty role_verification.method, non-empty role_verification.evidence, and return_schema_completed resolving to true.

send-to-gemini.js enforces deterministic schema validation per step: Step 0 requires start_of_turn with 5 specific string keys; Step 1 requires step_1_record with 5 string keys; Step 2 requires step_2_record with 4 string keys and stated_requirements as an array of non-empty strings; Step 3 requires Step_3 with 22 specific string keys, clause/modifier arrays, test results matching Test_Count, and strict Loop_Decision/return_to consistency; Step 4 requires Step_4 with user_request, timestamps, and completed/failed/not_completed action arrays.

The deterministic ground-truth engine verifies active run container nonces, reads Git HEAD commit, inspects structured evidence objects ({source, locator, observed_content}), and scans claim strings for repo paths and 40-character Git SHAs. File claims are verified against the local workspace and Git status/ls-files (matching verbatim observed text); Git SHAs are verified via git cat-file -e for blobs and commits. Findings with status CONTRADICTED, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, or NOT_EXECUTED are flagged as blocking, causing aggregate_status to become FAIL.

callGemini executes an HTTP POST to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent with an AbortSignal timeout of 180 seconds. The supervisor loop checks valid JSON, gate_result in {'PASS', 'FAIL'}, supervisor role verification, exact mirroring of execution keys in *_eval, exact mirroring of deterministic findings in ground_truth_verification_eval, and enforces that gate_result cannot be PASS if groundTruth.aggregate_status is not PASS; up to 4 attempts are allowed before throwing an error.

When gate_result is PASS, the step is added to completed_steps, current_step advances to the next remaining step (or null if complete, setting state.status to 'complete'), and last_supervisory_failure is deleted. When gate_result is FAIL, current_step remains unchanged, awaiting is set to { type: 'chatgpt_execution', step, reason: 'supervisory_gate_fail' }, status remains 'awaiting_chatgpt_execution', and state.last_supervisory_failure is recorded. State is persisted to state.json, messages.json, and store/store.json.
All 43 functions declared in send-to-gemini.js are invoked directly or indirectly during execution; there are no dead or unreferenced function declarations.

interpretations.statement: The implementation enforces ground-truth checks as a hard deterministic pre-condition: the Gemini model is programmatically prevented from granting a PASS gate whenever any empirical finding (file existence, exact text match, git object SHA) returns UNKNOWN, PARTIAL, NOT_EXECUTED, or CONTRADICTED.

While config.json provides path indirection for trigger_file, agents_file, runs_directory, and step3_evaluation_artifact, metadata fields ('version', 'description', and 'keys') are declarative documentation that is ignored by send-to-gemini.js, which hardcodes the Step 3 keys check for 'evaluation_heuristic' and 'step3_tsr'.

The runtime does not support dynamic function calling or Gemini tools. Interaction with the Gemini API is limited to raw prompt text and JSON schema repair dialogue; external tool execution by either agent does not exist in executable code.

The workflow commits changes only in ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/runs. The triggering file nextmessage/nextmessage.json is neither deleted, modified, nor staged during the commit step, leaving the repository with the latest trigger message committed on main.

truth_decisions.statement: The runtime executable implementation deterministically defines all trigger constraints, input schema validations for Steps 0–4, role control checks, ground-truth verifications against workspace files and Git objects, Gemini API invocation with repair retries, state machine advancement rules, and repository persistence operations.

There is no dead function or unimplemented code path inside send-to-gemini.js, although config.json contains descriptive and schema-checking properties ('version', 'description', 'keys') that are unused by the runtime loader.

unresolved_questions: Whether GEMINI_API_KEY in the GitHub repository is populated under GitHub Actions Variables ('vars') or Secrets ('secrets'), since gemini-chat.yml strictly reads ${{ vars.GEMINI_API_KEY }}.
